title: Community-acquired pneumonia in adults
instruction: Look at Texts A–D. Questions 1–7: which text? Questions 8–15: word/short phrase from the texts. Questions 16–20: complete the sentence. Spelling matters. Target: 15 minutes.
sharedWhichPrompt: In which text can you find information about

texts.label: A
texts.heading: CURB-65 severity assessment
texts.body:
One point is assigned for each of the following criteria:
• Confusion (new onset; Abbreviated Mental Test Score ≤8, or new disorientation in person, place, or time)
• Urea >7 mmol/L
• Respiratory rate ≥30 breaths/min
• Blood pressure: systolic <90 mmHg or diastolic ≤60 mmHg
• Age ≥65 years

Score interpretation
• 0–1: low severity — consider home treatment with oral antibiotics if social circumstances are safe
• 2: moderate severity — consider hospital admission for supervised assessment and treatment
• 3–5: high severity — urgent hospital admission required; consider ICU assessment if score 4–5

CURB-65 guides but does not replace clinical judgement. A score of 0 or 1 does not preclude admission if the patient is hypoxic, unable to take oral medication, or lacks adequate home support. Reassess all patients within 24 hours if there is any clinical deterioration.

texts.label: B
texts.heading: Empirical antibiotic therapy
texts.body:
Low severity (CURB-65 0–1)
• First choice: amoxicillin 500 mg orally three times daily for 5 days
• Penicillin allergy: clarithromycin 500 mg orally twice daily for 5 days

Moderate severity (CURB-65 2)
• First choice: amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily plus clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily (both oral) for 5 days
• Penicillin allergy: doxycycline 200 mg loading dose then 100 mg once daily for 5 days

High severity (CURB-65 3–5)
• First choice: co-amoxiclav 1.2 g IV three times daily plus clarithromycin 500 mg IV twice daily
• Penicillin allergy: levofloxacin 500 mg IV twice daily; seek microbiology advice if atypical organism suspected
• Switch to oral therapy when apyrexial for ≥24 hours, tolerating diet, and clinically improving; total course 7–10 days

Always send blood cultures before starting IV antibiotics. Review culture results at 48–72 hours and de-escalate to narrower-spectrum agents where culture and sensitivity permit.

texts.label: C
texts.heading: Investigations and oxygen targets
texts.body:
All patients
• Chest X-ray to confirm the diagnosis and document the extent of consolidation
• Full blood count, C-reactive protein, urea and electrolytes, liver function tests, blood glucose
• Pulse oximetry on arrival; repeat at least every 4 hours until readings are stable

Moderate or severe CAP (CURB-65 ≥2)
• Two sets of blood cultures before antibiotics are given
• Sputum Gram stain and culture if purulent sputum is produced
• Urinary pneumococcal antigen test (send regardless of prior antibiotic exposure)
• Urinary Legionella antigen if cluster, recent travel, or CURB-65 ≥3
• Arterial blood gas if SpO₂ <94% or clinical respiratory failure is suspected

Oxygen therapy targets
Aim for SpO₂ 94–98% in most patients. Use a lower target of 88–92% in patients known or suspected to be at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure (e.g. COPD or neuromuscular disease). Document the target on the oxygen prescription and reassess every 30 minutes until the patient is stable.

texts.label: D
texts.heading: Discharge criteria and follow-up
texts.body:
Criteria for discharge — all must be met
• Temperature <37.8°C on two consecutive observations ≥6 hours apart
• Heart rate <100 beats/min and respiratory rate <24 breaths/min
• Systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg
• SpO₂ ≥94% breathing air (or at the patient's documented home baseline)
• Able to take oral medication and tolerating diet and fluids
• Adequate community support and follow-up arrangements confirmed

Safety-net advice
Advise patients to return urgently if breathlessness worsens, temperature rises again, chest pain develops, or haemoptysis occurs. Provide written information on warning signs.

Follow-up
Arrange a follow-up chest X-ray at 6 weeks for patients who smoke, are aged ≥50 years, or have persisting symptoms, to exclude an underlying malignancy. Send a discharge summary to the GP documenting the organism identified (if any), the antibiotic course given, and allergy information recorded during the admission.

gist: Q1–7 = which text (scan headings and unique clinical markers).
Q8–15 = copy exact words or numbers from the relevant text.
Q16–20 = gap-fill: identify the precise term or value from the texts.
